# Slice 2 — App

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or
> superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for
> tracking.

**Goal:** Make the **App** type real: a small self-contained web app generated by a **separate call with
thinking OFF**, audited against the contract, **fact-verified before the card appears**, served from an
authenticated route with a strict CSP into `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts">`, persisted through a
`postMessage` bridge onto `artifact_kv`, shown in the card with Preview/Code, downloadable as `.html`, and
covered by the P1 eval suite rerun as a **regression gate**.

**Architecture:** The generator is its own server service under the artifact boundary
(`artifacts/app/`), never the chat turn: it makes one model call with thinking pinned off, extracts one
`html` fence, runs the static contract audit, optionally runs a fact-verification pass, and only then writes
the artifact — so the card the user sees is always post-verification. The app runs in an opaque-origin
iframe; its only privileged capability is `window.alfy.storage`, which is a bootstrap this app injects before
the model's own scripts and which speaks to the parent over `postMessage`; the parent translates those
messages into scoped `artifact_kv` reads and writes. No global in the frame can read the session, and no
message from the frame can name another artifact.

**Tech Stack:** SvelteKit + Svelte 5 runes, Drizzle on better-sqlite3, the repo's existing model-run path
(`normal-chat-model/`) and provider-model runtime defaults, Shiki 4 (already a dependency) for the Code tab,
Vitest, Playwright (headless Chromium with requests blocked, as the prototype did), Biome, Fallow.

**Spec:** [`-artifacts-spec.md`](./claude-at-home-2-artifacts-spec.md) §2.9–§2.11, §3 (App body), §4 (App
generation + the eval suites), §5 (the sandbox), §6 (Slice 2), §8.6. Reference implementation and evidence:
`.claude/worktrees/agent-afcaa6f617ee84abe/scripts/prototype-artifact-apps/` (`system-prompt.ts` — the
contract; `model.ts` — sampling and the thinking switch; `extract.ts` — fence extraction and the 15 static
checks; `score.ts` — the verdict; `evaluate.ts`, `gallery.ts`, `run.ts`; `README.md` — the results and the
hand audit) and the App frame of
[`-artifacts-mockups.html`](./claude-at-home-2-artifacts-mockups.html).

## Global Constraints

- **Node 22 only.** Prefix every npm/npx/vitest/playwright call with
  `export PATH=/opt/homebrew/opt/node@22/bin:$PATH`.
- **Thinking is OFF for the App call, always, regardless of the user's chat setting.** The prototype's phase A
  spent the entire 24,000-token budget on the reasoning channel twice and returned **empty content**
  (`finish_reason=length`, 88k and 90k characters of reasoning). Express it through the repo's existing
  thinking plumbing (`provider-model-runtime-defaults.ts` and the model-run path) — **do not hand-roll
  `chat_template_kwargs` in a new service** (AGENTS.md forbids duplicating that projection).
- **The answer is the app and nothing else** (spec §2.11). No tool calls, no clarifying questions, no file
  exploration. A `finish_reason=tool_calls` or an undeclared tool call is a **retry**, and it is recorded —
  the prototype saw exactly this reflex ("Let me first explore the project structure", 147 completion tokens,
  no tools declared).
- **Facts are verified before the App is shown** (spec §2.10). Three of ten prototype apps shipped a quiet
  content bug the automated verdict called `works`: a cumulative table labelled per-year, a plural gloss among
  singulars, and one wrong quiz answer key. Verification is not optional and its uncertainty is surfaced, not
  hidden.
- **The sandbox is not a preview.** The App runs in an opaque-origin iframe with a strict CSP served from an
  authenticated route — **not** through the existing uploaded-HTML `srcdoc` preview path
  (`DocumentPreviewRenderer.svelte:206`, which allows `allow-scripts allow-popups
  allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox` for the user's *own* file). A `srcdoc` document cannot carry a CSP header,
  and a model-authored app needs one.
- **No sharing, ever** (spec §2.16). An App is reachable only by its owner, and a message from a frame names
  no artifact: the artifact id comes from the route, never from the payload.
- **"Artifact" is never shown in the UI** (ADR-0066): the type is **App / Alkalmazás**.
- **Ownership:** every read and write goes through the `artifacts/` facade and its scope; the `artifact_kv`
  access is scoped by the artifact the route already authorised. **No new `ALLOWED_WITHOUT_SCOPE` exemption.**
- **Schema: no new table and no migration in this slice.** The App's body is the existing `artifacts.content_text`
  (`src/lib/server/db/schema.ts:352`) and its state is Slice 0's `artifact_kv`. Say so in the report, and check it
  instead of asserting it: `drizzle/meta/_journal.json`'s last entry is idx 123
  (`1777140000110_drop_home_suggestion_events`, 124 entries total), so the next free number after Slice 0's
  `1777140000111_artifacts_spine` is **`1777140000112` / idx 125 — and this slice must not claim it**. Run
  `npm run check:migrations` at the end and report it unchanged; a diff that adds a migration file is a bug in
  this slice.
- **The `.html` export is inert.** An App's HTML may only ever execute in the sandboxed frame. Never serve it
  through the existing same-origin HTML paths: `STANDARD_REPORT_PREVIEW_CSP`
  (`src/lib/server/services/file-serving-response-policy.ts:25`) allows `script-src 'unsafe-inline'` on a
  *renderer-produced* report, which is fine for a report and fatal for model-authored HTML, and
  `DocumentPreviewRenderer.svelte:206`'s `srcdoc` sandbox is a different contract. The download route is
  `Content-Disposition: attachment` (`file-serving-response-policy.ts:81`), so the bytes leave the app inert.
- **Cost is visible** (§8.6): the generation call and the verification call both appear in the existing cost
  display as their own model runs, not as part of the chat turn's cost.
- **Svelte 5 only** in touched files; no new legacy syntax. **Icons** from `@lucide/svelte` only. Verified present
  in the installed package (`node_modules/@lucide/svelte/dist/icons/`): `app-window`, `eye`, `code`, `download`,
  `history`, `refresh-cw`, `check`, `triangle-alert`, `layout-grid` (`layout-grid` is Slice 0's count button).
  Use `size={16} strokeWidth={1.75}` and `aria-hidden="true"` on decorative icons, as the other chat surfaces do.
- **i18n:** EN + HU for every `artifacts.app.*` key in the table below, appended to Slice 0's
  `src/lib/i18n/artifacts.ts`. `"artifacts."` is already in `AUDITED_PREFIXES` (Slice 0 adds it in
  `src/lib/i18n.test-helpers.ts`, whose `I18N_MODULES` list is at `:7-15`) — **do not add a `chat.artifacts.`
  prefix**: this slice has no such key, and an audited prefix with no keys is noise. The naming rule is about
  **values**: Slice 0's `src/lib/i18n/artifacts.test.ts` asserts no value in either locale matches `/artifact/i`
  (the keys are namespaced `artifacts.*`, which is the module's name and never user-visible, exactly as
  `fork.errors.requiredArtifact*` already coexists with the chat dictionary — `src/lib/i18n/chat.ts:740,742`
  EN and `:1839,1841` HU carry no "artifact" in the text).
- **Commits:** small and focused, staged by explicit path, explaining the *why*; never a bare `git stash`;
  every message ends with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Never push.
- **`npm run lint` is broken** by nested worktrees — run `npx biome check src scripts tests` and say so.

**Read this before A9: the harness is not this slice's to invent.** Slice 0 creates the skeleton

directory), Slice 5 owns the finished harness (`slice-5.md:664-704`: `config.ts`, `client.ts`,

`--suite verification` (`slice-5.md:746`). Do not invent `apps` or `verify` — an unknown suite name is a
runner error, not a quiet alias. Output goes under `scripts/eval-artifact-contracts/results/`, gitignored

Record which of the two layouts it landed on in the report. **Do not create a second runner and do not rename
another slice's files.**

The committed prototype baseline is **10/10 `works`, 0 glitches, 0 broken** with the automated verdict — and
**3/10 with a hand-audited content bug**. Both numbers go in the slice report, and a landing zone that is worse
on either is a finding, not a rounding error.

## Review Focus

1. **Thinking leaking back on.** If the App call inherits the chat turn's thinking setting, the budget goes to
   the reasoning channel and the user gets an empty app. A1 asserts the request that leaves the process carries
   thinking off **even when the turn's setting is on**, and A9's live run is the end-to-end proof.
2. **The model's prose reaching the frame.** The contract says one fence and nothing else, but the answer is a
   model's. Extraction, the fence check, the retry and the "not an app" failure path are all A1's; a half-answer
   must produce a visible failure, never an empty card.
3. **A wrong fact shipped as a nice app.** This is the whole reason for §2.10. A3 asserts the three known bug
   classes are *caught*, and the card shows the verification state; A9 measures it.
4. **The bridge being a hole.** A message from the frame must not be able to read or write another artifact, a
   conversation, or a file. A4/A5 assert the artifact id comes from the route, that the parent checks
   `event.source`, that unknown keys and oversized values are refused, and that a message from a frame that is
   not this app's is ignored.
5. **`allow-same-origin` creeping into the sandbox.** With it, the app shares the app's origin and can call the
   API with the user's cookies. A4 asserts the exact sandbox attribute string and the CSP header, and fails on
   any tightening-by-loosening.
6. **A stale app after a regeneration.** An App edit is a regeneration; the frame must not keep rendering the
   old body from its own cache. A6.6 and A8.2 assert the frame reloads on a version change, and that the old
   version is still in the history.
7. **Eval drift unmeasured.** §8.1 makes the suite a gate per type. A9 runs it against the real model and
   compares to the prototype baseline — a lower score changes the design, it does not get explained away.
8. **Token drift between the contract and `app.css`.** The prototype's six token names were shorthand
   (`--pg`, `--el`, `--tx`, `--mu`, `--bd`, `--ac`); the real ones are `--surface-page`, `--surface-elevated`,
   `--text-primary`, `--text-muted`, `--border-default`, `--accent`. A generated app must use the **real**
   names, and a test must fail if the values drift (A2).
9. **The export becoming a second execution surface.** The App's HTML is the one model-authored document in the
   product, and the repo already has a **second, weaker** live-HTML path that it would fall into by accident:
   the shared preview runtime gives an `.html` blob `trustedRuntime: true` whenever its CSP matches the report
   profile (`preview-runtime/index.ts:303`, `:328-345`; the profile itself is
   `file-serving-response-policy.ts:25-26`), and `htmlPreviewSandbox` then renders it with
   `allow-scripts allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox` (`DocumentPreviewRenderer.svelte:205-209`,
   `srcdoc` at `preview-runtime/text/index.ts:35-38`). That is fine for a server-rendered report and for a
   user's own uploaded file; for model-authored HTML it is a second sandbox with **popups that escape** and no
   `allow-scripts`-only guarantee. So: the produced `.html` is served as a **download** (attachment,
   `no-store`, `file-serving-response-policy.ts:81`), and if its File card is ever previewed it must take the
   restricted branch (`RESTRICTED_PREVIEW_CSP`, `:22-23` → `trustedRuntime: false` → `sandbox=""`) rather than
   the report branch. The App runs in exactly one place, the AppFrame, with one contract. A4's exact-CSP
   assertion, A6.5's server-side-HTML assertion and this paragraph are what keep the three apart; the
   `file-serving-response-policy` decision itself is not this slice's file to change — if it needs one, that is
   a reported follow-up, not a quiet edit.
10. **A verification that cannot verify claiming it did.** The web half of the check needs `research_web`, which
   is registered only when a Parallel key is configured (`normal-chat-tools/index.ts:562`, `:552-559`). On a
   deployment without it, the verifier can still catch the arithmetic and labelling bugs (prototype bugs 03 and
   04) and **cannot** settle a fact (bug 07). It must say so, and the card must not print "Alfy checked the facts
   in this app" in that state (the `unavailable` verdict in Contracts and `artifacts.app.verify.unavailable`).

## Contracts

### The App contract prompt — `src/lib/server/services/artifacts/app/contract.ts`

The prototype's `system-prompt.ts` ships almost verbatim
(`.claude/worktrees/agent-afcaa6f617ee84abe/scripts/prototype-artifact-apps/system-prompt.ts`, 33 lines), with
exactly two corrections:

1. **The six tokens become the real names and values**, read from `src/app.css`:

```css
:root { --surface-page:#fafaf8; --surface-elevated:#f4f3ee; --text-primary:#1a1a1a; --text-muted:#6b6b6b;
        --border-default:rgba(0,0,0,.08); --accent:#c15f3c }
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root { --surface-page:#1a1a1a; --surface-elevated:#242424;
        --text-primary:#ececec; --text-muted:#a0a0a0; --border-default:rgba(255,255,255,.08); --accent:#d4836b } }
```

   Those are the real values, byte-for-byte (`src/app.css:104,105,115,116,123,134` for light and
   `:194,195,202,203,210,221` for dark — read them from the file, do not retype them from this document). Two
   traps when writing the drift test (T2):
   - `src/app.css` also remaps three of those names for incognito (`.stage--incognito`, `:262-266`). The app
     gets the **canonical** palette: it is generated once and cannot re-theme per conversation. Parse the
     `:root` block and the `prefers-color-scheme: dark` block, not "every occurrence of the name", or the test
     fails on a correct contract.
   - The font stacks stay **Helvetica/Georgia** on purpose: an iframe inherits nothing, so referencing
     `--font-sans`/`--font-serif` would silently fall back. Write that reason in a comment in the contract file,
     and exclude the fonts from the drift assertion (T2.3), or the next person will "fix" them.

2. **Rule 5 keeps `window.alfy.storage.get/set`** exactly as prototyped — the bootstrap, not the model,
   provides it, and the contract's feature-detect sentence (`if (window.alfy && window.alfy.storage)`) is what
   keeps an app working in a plain browser where the bridge is absent.

`contract.ts` also exports the machine-readable mirror used by the audit and the tests:

```ts
export const APP_TOKENS: { name: string; light: string; dark: string }[];
export const APP_CONTRACT_RULES = [
	{ id: "no-script-src",        label: "No external scripts",            severity: "glitch" },
	{ id: "no-link-href",         label: "No external stylesheets or fonts", severity: "glitch" },
	{ id: "no-remote-img",        label: "No remote images",               severity: "glitch" },
	{ id: "no-network-api",       label: "No runtime network calls",       severity: "glitch" },
	{ id: "tokens",               label: "Defines all six tokens",         severity: "note" },
	{ id: "dark",                 label: "Dark mode via prefers-color-scheme", severity: "note" },
	{ id: "uses-vars",            label: "Actually uses the tokens",       severity: "note" },
	{ id: "no-hardcoded-extremes", label: "No #fff / #000 hardcoding",     severity: "note" },
	{ id: "georgia",              label: "Georgia for headings",           severity: "note" },
	{ id: "helvetica",            label: "Helvetica for UI text",          severity: "note" },
	{ id: "alfy-storage",         label: "Persists through window.alfy.storage", severity: "note" },
	{ id: "no-web-storage",       label: "No localStorage/sessionStorage/cookies", severity: "glitch" },
	{ id: "viewport",             label: "Viewport meta tag",              severity: "note" },
	{ id: "fluid",                label: "No fixed widths above 420px",    severity: "note" },
	{ id: "size",                 label: "Under ~400 lines",               severity: "note" },
] as const;
```

The same file exports the prompt constant and the rule-id type, so the audit, the tests and the eval harness
cannot drift apart:

```ts
/** The App contract, verbatim from the prototype's system-prompt.ts with the two corrections above. */
export const APP_CONTRACT_PROMPT: string;

export type AppContractRuleId = (typeof APP_CONTRACT_RULES)[number]["id"];
export type AppContractSeverity = (typeof APP_CONTRACT_RULES)[number]["severity"]; // "glitch" | "note"

/** A required sampler needle per rule; see audit.ts. In the contract file so tests can assert coverage. */
export const APP_SAMPLING_DEFAULTS = { temperature: 0.6, topP: 0.95, topK: 20, maxOutputTokens: 24_000 } as const;
export const APP_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS = APP_SAMPLING_DEFAULTS.maxOutputTokens;

/** The rule ids a passing app must not trip, used by both audit.ts and the eval scorer. */
export const APP_GLITCH_RULE_IDS: readonly AppContractRuleId[];
```

**One name for one thing.** This slice calls the prompt constant `APP_CONTRACT_PROMPT`; the prototype calls its
file `system-prompt.ts` and Task A1's prose called it `APP_CONTRACT`. Fix the prose to the exported name rather
than exporting two aliases.

The **audit is advisory to the user, not a gate on showing the app**: a `glitch` is shown on the card (the
app attempted a network call, or uses web storage), a `note` is not surfaced. The prototype's `score.ts`
verdict vocabulary (`works` / `works-with-glitches` / `broken`) is the eval harness's, **not** the product's —
the product shows an app and, when there is one, a note.

### The audit — `src/lib/server/services/artifacts/app/audit.ts`

```ts
export interface ContractCheck {
	rule: AppContractRuleId;
	severity: AppContractSeverity;
	passed: boolean;
	/** One short, user-safe sentence, or null when the check passed. Never contains the app's HTML. */
	detail: string | null;
}

/** Pure, synchronous, never throws. Returns one entry per APP_CONTRACT_RULES row, in that order. */
export function auditAppHtml(html: string): ContractCheck[];
```

Rules the audit keeps, ported from the prototype's `extract.ts` (`contractChecks`) rather than reinvented:

- **All fifteen run, always.** A check whose needle is absent returns `passed: false`; the function does not
  early-return, because the card shows more than one glitch when there is more than one.
- **The needle set is the check.** `<script src>`, `<link href>` to an `http(s)` URL, remote `<img src>`, the six
  network APIs (`fetch(`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `WebSocket`, `EventSource`, `sendBeacon`, `@import`), the four
  web-storage APIs (`localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, `document.cookie`, `indexedDB`), the six tokens defined, a
  `prefers-color-scheme: dark` block, ≥ 5 `var(--` references, **exact** `#fff`/`#ffffff`/`#000`/`#000000`
  literals only, Georgia, Helvetica, `alfy.storage`, the viewport meta, fixed widths above 420 px, and ≤ 460
  lines. Copy the prototype's regexes; a "tidy-up" here changes what the product calls a glitch.
- **Detection is per-rule and independent of the model's prose** — the audit sees only the extracted HTML.
- **The five `glitch` rules map to three user-visible messages** (Contracts → i18n):
  `no-network-api` → `artifacts.app.glitch.network`; `no-web-storage` → `artifacts.app.glitch.storage`; and
  `no-script-src` + `no-link-href` + `no-remote-img` → `artifacts.app.glitch.external`, because all three end the
  same way for the user: the app was built to load something from outside and CSP `default-src 'none'` refuses
  it, so it renders incomplete. **Do not collapse the rules** — the eval harness scores them separately.
- **A `note` never reaches the UI.** It is recorded, it goes in the eval result, and it is available to the
  slice report; it is not rendered on the card.
- **The audit never rejects.** There is no path from `auditAppHtml` to "do not show the app" — the Product
  Decision is Owner decision 9 (a glitch is shown, a note is not).

### Generation — `src/lib/server/services/artifacts/app/generate.ts`

```ts
import type { ModelId } from "$lib/model-types";
import type { NormalChatModelRunUsage } from "$lib/server/services/normal-chat-model";
import type { ThinkingMode } from "$lib/reasoning-depth-types";

export interface AppGenerationRequest {
	userId: string;
	conversationId: string | null;
	/** The user's request, verbatim. The only thing from the session that reaches the model. */
	prompt: string;
	/** From the turn's own language detection (`services/language.ts`), not guessed here. */
	language: "en" | "hu";
	/** When the caller already knows it (a regeneration keeps the old title unless the user renamed it). */
	title?: string | null;
	/** The chat model this turn is using; the App call defaults to "model1" and never inherits thinking. */
	modelId?: ModelId;
	abortSignal?: AbortSignal;
}

/** The prototype's vocabulary, kept: which of its three extraction paths produced the HTML. */
export type AppExtractionStrategy = "fence" | "recovered-document" | "empty";

export type AppGenerationFailureReason =
	| "empty_content"
	| "no_fence"
	| "tool_call"
	| "too_long"
	| "provider_error";

export type AppGenerationResult =
	| {
			ok: true;
			html: string;
			/** `<title>`, then `<h1>`, then a truncated prompt. Never the word "Artifact". */
			title: string;
			/** "fence" for a contract-shaped answer; "recovered-document" when a whole document was recovered. */
			extraction: AppExtractionStrategy;
			fences: number;
			checks: ContractCheck[];
			/** Both attempts' usage summed; the cost display wants what this feature actually spent. */
			usage: NormalChatModelRunUsage;
			attempts: number;
			/** Non-fatal observations for the report and the eval harness — never shown to the user. */
			warnings: string[];
	  }
	| { ok: false; reason: AppGenerationFailureReason; detail: string; usage: NormalChatModelRunUsage | null; attempts: number };

/** The only thinking setting this feature ever uses. Typed so a later "make it configurable" reads as a change. */
export const APP_THINKING_MODE: ThinkingMode = "off";

/** One retry, as the prototype: a second failure is reported as itself, not retried again. */
export const APP_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 2;
```

**Which model path.** The generator is a **consumer** of `normal-chat-model/` and must not reimplement any of
its policy (`AGENTS.md`, and `normal-chat-model/`'s own contract):

```ts
import { getConfig } from "$lib/server/config-store";
import {
	buildNormalChatModelRunProviderOptions,
	resolveNormalChatModelRunProvider,
	runStreamingNormalChatModelRun,
} from "$lib/server/services/normal-chat-model";

const runtimeConfig = getConfig();                                    // config-store.ts:1372, override-aware
const provider = await resolveNormalChatModelRunProvider(             // normal-chat-model/index.ts:377
	params.modelId ?? "model1",
	runtimeConfig,
);

for await (const event of runStreamingNormalChatModelRun({            // normal-chat-model/index.ts:1353
	provider,
	modelId: params.modelId ?? "model1",
	runtimeConfig,
	system: APP_CONTRACT_PROMPT,
	messages: [{ role: "user", content: buildAppRequestMessage(params) }],
	// The thinking switch is this one call. "off" is a ThinkingMode (reasoning-depth-types.ts), and the
	// provider-specific shape of "thinking disabled" is the compatibility layer's job:
	// provider-compatibility.ts:617-660 (resolveThinkingType / the qwen branch).
	resolveProviderOptions: (attemptProvider) =>
		buildNormalChatModelRunProviderOptions(attemptProvider, APP_THINKING_MODE),
	maxOutputTokens: APP_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS,
	abortSignal: params.abortSignal,
})) { /* accumulate text_delta; read finish; take usage */ }
```

- **Do not add a sampling parameter to `normal-chat-model/`.** `provider-compatibility.ts:203-207` already carries
  the qwen family's `defaultSampling: { temperature: 0.6, topP: 0.95, topK: 20 }` — the prototype's values — and
  the run path applies it (`:1286-1288`, `:1600-1602`). The generator asserts the prototype's numbers **at the
  provider-request boundary** (T1.2) and adds nothing to the shared signature. If the deployed provider is one
  where those values do not apply, that is a provider-configuration fact for the report, not a new parameter.
- **`max_tokens` is the one value this feature owns**: `APP_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS = 24_000`, passed as
  `maxOutputTokens`, because the contract promises an app and the prototype's 12.7–23.0 s answers fit inside it.
  **Take the smaller of it and the model's own cap, explicitly.** The run path does
  `maxOutputTokens: params.maxOutputTokens ?? params.provider.maxOutputTokens` (`normal-chat-model/index.ts:1285`
  plain, `:1599` streaming) — a caller's value **replaces** the provider-model default rather than being capped
  by it, and that default is the model's configured `maxTokens` (`:531-534`, from
  `provider-model-runtime-defaults.ts:87-92`). So pass
  `Math.min(APP_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS, provider.maxOutputTokens ?? APP_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS)`: asking for more than the
  configured model can emit is how `finish_reason=length` arrives, which is the failure this slice already
  detects but should not manufacture.
- **`top_k` is dropped and retried if the endpoint rejects it** (the prototype's `allowDropTopK`): on a 400 naming
  `top_k`, re-issue the same call once without `providerOptions` sampling rather than failing the generation.
  Record it in `warnings`.
- **Streamed, and that is not a preference**: an answer this size behind a proxy response timeout does not return
  (`model.ts` in the prototype learned it; `runStreamingNormalChatModelRun` also owns the first-output timeout,
  `:1379-1400`).
- **Retry once** (`APP_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 2`) on a transport failure, empty content, `finish_reason=length`, an
  undeclared tool call, or `finish_reason=tool_calls`. `attempts` and `warnings` record every attempt, because
  "the model tried to explore the project" is a finding about the contract, not noise.
- **Extraction:** `extractAppHtml` (prototype `extract.ts`) with its three strategies. A missing fence is
  `no_fence` **after** the retry — do not accept a whole-document answer without a fence, and do not pick a
  different fence tag. Read `extract.ts` for the exact strategy vocabulary before writing a second one; only
  `strategy: "empty"` becomes `empty_content`.
- **The prompt is assembled from the request only**: `APP_CONTRACT_PROMPT` as the system message, and one user
  message carrying the request plus the language instruction. No chat history, no other artifact, no memory, no
  user display name — assert it byte-for-byte (A1.6).
- The generator **does not write the artifact**. It returns; the caller (the tool, or the regenerate route)
  decides, after verification, to persist. That ordering is what makes "verified before the card appears" true.
- **Every call is recorded for cost** (§8.6): map `usage` through
  `mapNormalChatModelRunUsageToProviderSnapshot` (exported from `normal-chat-model/`) and record it as its own
  model run with a feature-scoped id — the precedent is `recordControlModelUsage`
  (`analytics.ts:2630`, synthetic `control:<feature>:<uuid>` message ids at `:2698`), which is what makes
  `getConversationCostSummary` (`analytics.ts:2723-2740`) show it. App generation never inflates the chat turn's
  token counts.


### Fact verification — `src/lib/server/services/artifacts/app/verify.ts`

The prototype has **no implementation of this**; it has the evidence that it is needed (three hand-audited
content bugs, `README.md`). This is new work, and its design is deliberately conservative:

```ts
import type { JsonControlMessageUsage } from "$lib/server/services/normal-chat-control-model";

/** One shape for both call kinds, so the cost display does not learn two vocabularies. */
export interface AppModelCallUsage {
	promptTokens: number;
	completionTokens: number;
	totalTokens: number;
	cachedInputTokens?: number;
}

/** The three measured prototype bug classes, plus everything the verifier is sure about but cannot name. */
export type AppVerificationFindingClass =
	| "wrong_key"
	| "mislabelled_aggregate"
	| "wrong_unit"
	| "other";

export interface AppVerificationFinding {
	/** The claim as it appears in the app, quoted and shortened. Goes into Alfy's note, so: no HTML, no markup. */
	claim: string;
	/** One sentence, in the request's language, saying what is wrong. */
	problem: string;
	class: AppVerificationFindingClass;
	/** Where it is: a table column label, a question id, a heading. Null when the claim has no single home. */
	location: string | null;
	/** false when the verifier could not settle it — the honest half of "uncertain". */
	settled: boolean;
}

export type AppVerificationVerdict =
	| "clean"        // checkable, checked, nothing wrong
	| "repaired"     // checkable, something was wrong, the repair is in repairedHtml and re-verified
	| "uncertain"    // checkable, something may be wrong, and no repair was safe to make
	| "unavailable"; // the check could not run to the standard it claims (no web search; a call failed)

export interface AppVerification {
	/** false when the classifier said there is nothing checkable (a timer, a colour picker). */
	checked: boolean;
	verdict: AppVerificationVerdict;
	findings: AppVerificationFinding[];
	/** The app with the repairs applied, when the verdict is "repaired", and the claim list is unchanged. */
	repairedHtml: string | null;
	/** Non-null whenever any model call happened: classifier, verifier and repair summed. */
	usage: AppModelCallUsage | null;
	/** The user-facing reason for "uncertain"/"unavailable", in the request's language; null otherwise. */
	reason: string | null;
}

export async function verifyApp(params: {
	userId: string;
	conversationId: string | null;
	html: string;
	prompt: string;
	language: "en" | "hu";
	abortSignal?: AbortSignal;
}): Promise<AppVerification>;
```

**What it checks.** Two calls, in this order, both with thinking off:

1. **The classifier** — `sendJsonControlMessage(html, "model2", { … })`
   (`normal-chat-control-model.ts:336-340`), a structured-output control call (no tools, `jsonSchema` with
   `strict: true`, `JsonControlResponseSchema` at `:27-31`), answering
   `{ checkable: boolean, kinds: ("table" | "answer_key" | "computed_numbers" | "dates" | "unit_conversion" | "named_facts")[] }`.
   A separate call because the App contract forbids text outside the fence, so the generator cannot declare
   anything about its own content (§2.11); `checkable: false` ends the pass here and costs nothing more.
2. **The verifier** — a bounded run through the model-run path with **exactly one tool**, `research_web`, which
   is the one place a tool is allowed in this slice and is a verifier tool, never the generator's. It checks
   each claim in the app against the request and against arithmetic:
   - **computed numbers**: recompute them from the app's own inputs; a total that is not the sum, a percentage
     that is not the ratio, a running total presented as a per-period figure (the prototype's bug 03 —
     `mislabelled_aggregate`);
   - **labels and units**: does the label describe the column, does the gloss agree in number and language with
     its neighbours (bug 04 — `wrong_unit`, `frog` rendered among plural `békák`);
   - **answer keys**: is the keyed answer actually the correct one for the question as written (bug 07 —
     `wrong_key`, Bucharest);
   - **real-world facts** (`named_facts`): settled with `research_web` where it is configured, never from the
     model's memory alone — a fact asserted from memory is exactly the failure mode being fixed.

**What it does when it fails.**

- A **clear error** is repaired **once** and re-verified. `repairedHtml` carries the whole repaired document;
  the finding is kept in `findings` with `settled: true`; the verdict is `repaired`.
- A repair is only accepted if the claim list **did not gain a claim**. Compare the claim lists; a repair that
  introduces one is `uncertain` with the original HTML — never "clean". (A repair that *rewrites* a claim is
  allowed; a repair that *adds* one is a new, unverified assertion.)
- A claim the verifier cannot settle — no web search configured (`parallelConfigured` is false,
  `normal-chat-tools/index.ts:562`), or a claim it is not sure about — yields `settled: false` and a verdict of
  `uncertain` (or `unavailable` when **nothing** could be checked to the promised standard).
- A failed or timed-out verification call yields `unavailable` with `reason`, never `clean`. The app still
  ships: a verification that did not run must not be mistaken for a verification that passed.
- `findings` is never empty on `uncertain`/`unavailable` **when a finding was made**; when the cause is "could
  not check", `reason` carries it and `findings` stays empty. Both states are legal — the card shows `reason`
  for the first and the findings for the second.

**What the user sees.** The verdict maps to one line on the card and, when there are findings, to Alfy's own
comment on the artifact (§2.8) — one comment per verification pass, not one per finding:

| verdict | card line (EN / HU key) | Alfy's note |
|---|---|---|
| `checked: false` | nothing | none |
| `clean` | `artifacts.app.verify.clean` | none |
| `repaired` | `artifacts.app.verify.repaired` | one comment naming what was fixed |
| `uncertain` | `artifacts.app.verify.uncertain` | one comment quoting each unsettled finding |
| `unavailable` | `artifacts.app.verify.unavailable` | none (there is nothing to quote) |

- The verifier must **never** silently rewrite a fact: a rewrite is a repair, a repair is a finding, and a
  finding is visible. The prototype's failure mode was a confident-looking wrong app; the fix is visible doubt.
- Both calls count in the cost display as their own model runs (§8.6), attributed like the generation call.

### The sandbox route and the bridge

**The served route** — `src/routes/api/artifacts/[id]/app/+server.ts`. `GET` only; no other method, and no
`?redirect=`/`?theme=` parameters that would make the response vary.

```ts
export const GET: RequestHandler = async (event) => {
	try {
		requireAuth(event);
	} catch {
		// requireAuth throws a redirect (auth/hooks.ts:12-18); a fetch-driven route answers 401 instead,
		// which is the existing idiom at routes/api/campaign-assets/[id]/content/+server.ts:6-11.
		return json({ error: "Unauthorized" }, { status: 401 });
	}
	const artifact = await getArtifact({ userId: event.locals.user.id, artifactId: event.params.id });
	if (!artifact || artifact.kind !== "app" || typeof artifact.body !== "string") {
		// 404 for a foreign artifact, a foreign id, a deleted one, or a non-App kind — never a 403 that
		// confirms an id exists (slice-0.md:316 sets the same rule for the family).
		return json({ error: "Not found" }, { status: 404 });
	}
	return new Response(injectAppBootstrap(artifact.body), { status: 200, headers: APP_SANDBOX_HEADERS });
};
```

Headers, as one exported constant so the test asserts the same object the route sends
(`Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Cache-Control: no-store`, and the
CSP below). The `?v=` the frame passes is a cache-buster and **must not** be trusted as a version selector: the
body always comes from the artifact row.

- **CSP header, exactly this string** (checked in T4 as a string assertion so a later edit cannot quietly weaken
  it):

```
sandbox allow-scripts;
default-src 'none';
script-src 'unsafe-inline';
style-src 'unsafe-inline';
img-src data: blob:;
font-src 'none';
connect-src 'none';
form-action 'none';
base-uri 'none';
frame-ancestors 'self'
```

  - `'unsafe-inline'` for script and style is required because the contract mandates inline `<style>`/`<script>`
    and a nonce cannot be applied to model-authored markup. It is safe **because** the frame is opaque-origin,
    `connect-src 'none'` and `default-src 'none'`: the app cannot fetch, cannot read a cookie, cannot load a
    font or a remote image, and cannot reach another origin.
  - `sandbox allow-scripts` is this slice's addition, and it is the **defence in depth for the
    direct-open case**: a user who pastes the route URL into a tab gets the same opaque-origin document the
    frame gets, with no cookie access and no `localStorage` — instead of a same-origin HTML page running
    model-authored script with the session. It is belt to the frame's braces; the frame attribute is the brace.
    The repo already serves untrusted-ish content this way (`campaign-assets/[id]/content/+server.ts:28-32`
    sends `sandbox; default-src 'none'; …` for an SVG), so the directive is house style, not an invention.
    If A4.5's forged-message test shows the bridge cannot message under it (it should not — an opaque origin may
    still `postMessage` its parent), the fix is to drop **nothing** from this header and nothing from the frame
    attribute: re-derive why, and say so in the report.
  - `frame-ancestors 'self'` keeps the app embeddable in the app and nowhere else. It is not the sandbox: the
    `<iframe sandbox>` attribute is what makes the frame opaque-origin.

- **Why `allow-same-origin` must never appear — in the CSP directive or in the frame attribute.** With it the
  app is served from (and the document runs on) the app's own origin: `document.cookie` is the user's session
  cookie, `fetch('/api/…')` is an authenticated request, `localStorage` is the app's, and the frame could call
  any API the user can. `allow-scripts` **plus** `allow-same-origin` on a same-origin document is equivalent to
  no sandbox at all — the two together are the classic escape. The attribute is therefore asserted as an exact
  string (A4.4) and the CSP as an exact string (A4.2), and the parent additionally requires `event.origin ===
  "null"` (see the frame), so a same-origin regression fails at runtime as well as in the tests.

- The server **injects the bootstrap** immediately after `<head>` (before any model-authored script), exactly
  as the prototype injected its storage mock before the app's own scripts. Injection is a string splice at the
  first `<head>`; a document without `<head>` gets the bootstrap prepended to the body. The bootstrap is a
  **server-owned constant** (`app/bootstrap.ts`), never built from the artifact's content — no interpolation, no
  template, no `JSON.stringify` of anything from the artifact.

**The bootstrap** (a small IIFE, no dependencies):

```js
(function () {
  var seq = 0, waiting = {};
  function call(method, args) {
    return new Promise(function (resolve, reject) {
      var id = ++seq;
      waiting[id] = { resolve: resolve, reject: reject };
      window.parent.postMessage({ v: 1, kind: "alfy.storage", id: id, method: method, args: args }, "*");
      setTimeout(function () { if (waiting[id]) { delete waiting[id]; reject(new Error("alfy.storage timed out")); } }, 5000);
    });
  }
  Object.defineProperty(window, "alfy", {
    value: { storage: {
      get: function (k) { return call("get", [String(k)]); },
      set: function (k, v) { return call("set", [String(k), v]); }
    } },
    writable: false, configurable: false, enumerable: true
  });
})();
```

`postMessage(..., "*")` is deliberate and safe here: the parent has an opaque-origin child, so the target
origin cannot be named. The **parent** is where the trust decision is made.

Three properties of the bootstrap that the tests pin (A4.3):

- **It is injected first and it is non-configurable.** `Object.defineProperty` with `writable: false,
  configurable: false` means a model-authored `window.alfy = {…}` (the contract's rule 5 shows the app how to
  feature-detect, and a model can still try to define it) silently does nothing in the frame's non-strict
  script, and `delete window.alfy` fails too. The app can extend `window.alfy.storage` if it wants; it cannot
  remove or replace the bridge.
- **A missing key resolves to `null`, not a rejection** — the parent answers `{ ok: true, value: null }`
  (A5.5), because the contract's `const saved = await window.alfy.storage.get('my-key')  // or null` is a
  promise of a value.
- **A timeout rejects the app's promise** after 5 s with no reply (the frame never answered, or the parent
  refused), and the contract's feature-detect keeps the app alive. The rejection message is fixed text from the
  bootstrap constant; it never carries the key or the value.

**The frame** — `src/lib/components/artifacts/app/AppFrame.svelte`:

```ts
interface Props {
	artifactId: string;
	/** Changes when a new version is written, so the frame reloads rather than rendering a stale app. */
	version: number;
	onStorageError?: (message: string) => void;
}
```

- Renders `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" src="/api/artifacts/{artifactId}/app?v={version}" title={…}>` —
  **exactly** `allow-scripts`, as a literal string in the component. No `allow-same-origin`, no
  `allow-popups`, no `allow-forms`, no `allow-top-navigation`, no `allow-modals`, no
  `allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox` (the literal at `DocumentPreviewRenderer.svelte:206` is the uploaded-file
  contract, not this one).
- `bind:this` on the iframe is `$state<HTMLIFrameElement | null>(null)` (Svelte 5 runes: a ref read by a
  handler is state). The `message` listener is attached in an action or `$effect` and **removed on unmount**;
  a listener left on `window` after the card closes is how a stale frame keeps a storage channel open.
- `version` is the artifact's `versionNumber` from the artifact detail; on change the iframe's `src` changes
  (same `?v=`), which reloads the frame rather than showing the previous body from the browser cache —
  `Cache-Control: no-store` on the route is what makes the reload honest.

**The trust boundary — the whole of it.** The wire shapes are fixed; everything else is ignored:

```ts
// frame → parent
type AlfiStorageRequest = { v: 1; kind: "alfy.storage"; id: number; method: "get" | "set"; args: unknown[] };
// parent → frame
type AlfiStorageReply =
	| { v: 1; kind: "alfy.storage.result"; id: number; ok: true; value: unknown }
	| { v: 1; kind: "alfy.storage.result"; id: number; ok: false; error: string };
```

A request is served **only** when all five hold; anything else is dropped without a reply:

```ts
const frame = iframe;                                        // the bound element
if (!frame || !frame.contentWindow) return;                  // not loaded, or gone
if (event.source !== frame.contentWindow) return;            // a different window (a popup, a sibling, the opener)
if (event.origin !== "null") return;                         // the frame stopped being opaque-origin: fail closed
const data = event.data;
if (!data || typeof data !== "object") return;
if (data.v !== 1 || data.kind !== "alfy.storage") return;    // not our protocol (kind is the discriminator)
if (data.method !== "get" && data.method !== "set") return;
if (typeof data.id !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(data.id)) return;
if (!Array.isArray(data.args) || (data.args.length !== 1 && data.args.length !== 2)) return;
// The artifact id is the PROP. data.* is never read for it, and a message cannot name one.
const artifactId = props.artifactId;
```

Why each clause exists, and what it stops:

| Clause | The attack it stops |
|---|---|
| `event.source === frame.contentWindow` | Any other window posting into the page: a popup the app opened (it cannot open one — no `allow-popups` — but the check does not rely on that), another frame on the same page, an opener, or an injected script elsewhere in the app. |
| `event.origin === "null"` | The frame ceasing to be opaque-origin — i.e. `allow-same-origin` having been added, or the route being replaced by a same-origin `srcdoc`. The bridge **stops working** in that case, loudly, instead of handing the app its own origin's storage. |
| `kind === "alfy.storage"` (plus `v`) | A message from the same frame that is not this protocol — another feature's `postMessage`, an app's own chatter — being interpreted as a storage call. |
| `typeof data.id === "number"` | A reply id that is not a number, i.e. a payload the parent would echo back into something else. |
| **the artifact id is the prop** | The whole forgery class the caller asked about: a message whose payload says `{"artifactId": "<someone else's id>"}`. There is no code path that reads an id from `event.data` — so a frame cannot name another artifact, a conversation, a file, or a user, even if it forges every other field correctly. The kv route re-authorises `[id]` against the session anyway (A5.2), which is the second, server-side half of the same guarantee: the parent is not the only check. |
| one `args` array of length 1–2 | `set`'s value being spread into the call, or extra arguments reaching the server side. |

- **Replies go to `event.source.postMessage(reply, "*")`** — never `postMessage` on the window, never another
  target — so only the window that asked is answered.
- The parent refuses, with `ok: false` and one of the fixed messages, a key that is not a string, a `set` value
  that is not JSON-serialisable, a value over `APP_KV_LIMITS.maxValueBytes`, and a key count over
  `maxKeys`. Those refusals do not carry the value back into the frame, and the frame's `onStorageError` is
  called with the app's localised message only.
- **Nothing in this path logs a value.** The dev-only counter (below) counts rejected messages by clause; a
  stored value can be the user's own text and must not reach a log line, a console message or a telemetry row.
- A forged message from another window, a message with the wrong `kind`, a message with no id, a message before
  the frame loaded, and a message after it unmounted are all ignored **and** counted in a small dev-only
  diagnostic (`import.meta.env.DEV`), keyed by rejection clause. It is a counter, not a log.

**The server side of the bridge** — `src/lib/server/services/artifacts/app/storage.ts`:

```ts
import {
	ARTIFACT_KV_KEY_MAX_CHARS,
	ARTIFACT_KV_MAX_KEYS,
	ARTIFACT_KV_VALUE_MAX_BYTES,
} from "../limits";                                                    // Slice 0's constants, not copies

/**
 * The App-facing view of the store's limits. Three of the four come from Slice 0's
 * `limits.ts` (`slice-0.md:937-939`) because `kv.setKv` enforces them and slice 0
 * already assigned this slice the job of *surfacing* its refusals (`slice-0.md:993`).
 * `maxTotalBytes` is this slice's addition: the store caps one value and the key
 * count, so without a total an App could still hold 200 × 256 KiB.
 */
export const APP_KV_LIMITS = {
	maxKeys: ARTIFACT_KV_MAX_KEYS,                 // 200
	maxKeyLength: ARTIFACT_KV_KEY_MAX_CHARS,       // 128
	maxValueBytes: ARTIFACT_KV_VALUE_MAX_BYTES,    // 256 * 1024
	maxTotalBytes: 1024 * 1024,                    // this slice: 1 MiB of value_json per artifact
} as const;

export async function readAppValue(params: { userId: string; artifactId: string; key: string }): Promise<{ ok: true; value: unknown } | { ok: false; reason: "not_found" | "too_large" }>;
export async function writeAppValue(params: { userId: string; artifactId: string; key: string; value: unknown }): Promise<{ ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: "not_found" | "too_large" | "too_many_keys" | "not_serialisable" }>;
```

**Why the numbers are Slice 0's and not this slice's.** `kv.setKv` refuses over
`ARTIFACT_KV_MAX_KEYS`/`_KEY_MAX_CHARS`/`_VALUE_MAX_BYTES` and returns only a boolean
(`slice-0.md:462-463`), so this slice has to pre-check the same three bounds itself to have a reason to report —
and pre-checking a *different* number than the store would be a lie the app hears once and then the store
enforces silently. The five reasons (`invalid_key`, `too_large`, `too_many_keys`, `not_serialisable`,
`not_found`) are **this** layer's vocabulary: the store's `false` cannot distinguish them, and the bridge must.
A test asserts `APP_KV_LIMITS.maxKeys === ARTIFACT_KV_MAX_KEYS` and the same for the key and value caps, so a
later slice 0 change cannot drift away from the bridge's copy of the truth.

Reached from `POST /api/artifacts/[id]/app/kv` with `{ key, value }` (write) and
`GET /api/artifacts/[id]/app/kv?key=…` (read), both `requireAuth` + scope. **The artifact id is the route's**,
so a frame cannot address another artifact even if the parent were tricked. Values are `JSON.stringify`-ed into
`artifact_kv.value_json` with the size limits above enforced **before** the write; a value that is not
JSON-serialisable (a function, a cycle, a `BigInt`) is refused with `not_serialisable`, not thrown.

The routes, literally (thin, like every other route here — the limits live in `storage.ts`):

| Route | Request | OK | Refusals |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/artifacts/[id]/app/kv?key=…` | query `key` | `200 { ok: true, value }` (`value: null` for a missing key) | `400 { ok: false, reason: "invalid_key" }`; `404 { ok: false, reason: "not_found" }` |
| `POST /api/artifacts/[id]/app/kv` | `{ key: string, value: unknown }` | `200 { ok: true }` | `400 { ok: false, reason }`; `404` as above; `413 { ok: false, reason: "too_large" }`; `409 { ok: false, reason: "too_many_keys" }` |

`reason` is one of `"invalid_key" | "too_large" | "too_many_keys" | "not_serialisable" | "not_found"`, and it is
also the string the frame turns into a localised message (`artifacts.app.storage.*`). The response never echoes
the key or the value.

| Limit | Value | Where enforced |
|---|---|---|
| `maxKeys` | `ARTIFACT_KV_MAX_KEYS` (200) per artifact | `writeAppValue` counts the artifact's rows before calling `setKv`; the store enforces the same number again |
| `maxKeyLength` | `ARTIFACT_KV_KEY_MAX_CHARS` (128) characters | `writeAppValue` and `readAppValue`, before any read |
| `maxValueBytes` | `ARTIFACT_KV_VALUE_MAX_BYTES` (256 KiB) of `JSON.stringify(value)` (UTF-8) | `writeAppValue`, before the insert |
| `maxTotalBytes` | 1 MiB of `value_json` for the artifact | `writeAppValue`, summing the artifact's rows before the write — this is the cap that stops one app filling the database (`slice-0.md:937-939` caps a value and a count, never a total) |
| `not_serialisable` | — | `writeAppValue` wraps `JSON.stringify`; `undefined`, a function, a `BigInt` and a cycle are refused, never thrown |

- **Four checks, then one store call.** `writeAppValue` validates, then calls Slice 0's `kv.setKv({ userId,
  artifactId, key, valueJson })` and translates its `false` into `not_found` (the scoped read returned nothing).
  The count and the total are **read-then-write, not one transaction** — `setKv` owns its own transaction
  (`slice-0.md:462-463`) and this slice must not open a second one behind the facade. The worst case is one
  extra value over `maxTotalBytes` under two simultaneous writes from the same app: bounded by one value, no
  cross-user effect, and the store's own per-value and per-key caps still hold. **Say that in the code
  comment**; do not claim an atomicity the layering does not give.

- **The scope marker is not optional.** `artifact_kv` has no `user_id` column, so Slice 0's guard requires a kv
  reader to prove its artifact id came from a scoped read: read the artifact through `getArtifact({ userId, … })`
  first and pass **that** id down (`slice-0.md:465-470`, and the marker set at `slice-0.md:473`). A kv function
  that takes a bare `artifactId` from a request is exactly the pattern the containment test exists to catch —
  `tests/cross-cutting/incognito-artifact-containment.test.ts:561-567` (`readsGuardedTables`) and `:578-592`.
- **A write is an upsert on `(artifact_id, key)`** and refreshes `updated_at`; that is why the primary key in
  Slice 0's DDL is the pair (`slice-0.md:126-132`).
- **Regeneration does not touch kv** (Owner decision 5): the rows are keyed by artifact, not by version, and
  nothing in the regenerate path deletes them. A test asserts it rather than trusting the absence of code
  (A8.4).
- **Erasure and incognito containment come for free from the FK** (`ON DELETE CASCADE`,
  `slice-0.md:127`) but are asserted through the route paths, not raw SQL (A10.1, A10.2).

### The App card

`ArtifactCard.svelte` gains an `app` body (append-only, plan decision 21):

- **Preview** (default): `AppFrame` plus, under it, the app's own title and the verification note when there is
  one ("Alfy checked the numbers in this app" / "Alfy was not sure about one claim — see the note").
- **Code**: the stored HTML in a read-only Shiki-highlighted block (`lang: "html"`, the existing Shiki 4
  dependency and the existing `DocumentPreviewRenderer` styling path for code), with a copy affordance. Code is
  **read-only**: an App is edited by regenerating, not by typing in the HTML (spec §1: no in-app editing of
  generated content; ADR-0065's exception is Documents).
- **Download `.html`**: through the file-production engine (§5: `produce_file` stays the export engine) so the
  download lands on the canonical chat-file download route and appears as a File artifact with a normal card.
  **The HTML comes from the artifact row on the server, never from the client** — the request carries an id, and
  the server reads the body (assert it: A6.5). `inline_text` is **not** an option: `html` is deliberately
  excluded from the inline-text output types because an HTML request belongs to the report renderers
  (`src/lib/shared/file-types/production.ts:106-113`). `document_source` renders a report from structured
  source — also not a byte-copy. The one shape that can carry these exact bytes is **`program` mode**, whose
  intake accepts any non-empty `normalizeOutputTypes(parsed.outputs)` and a caller-authored source
  (`file-production/execution-adapter.ts:232-278`), with the HTML passed as a base64 string inside the program
  source so escaping is exact and the sandbox has no network to reach. The literal request to
  `POST /api/chat/files/produce` (`routes/api/chat/files/produce/+server.ts:78-103`, body shape pinned by
  `file-production/intake.ts:472-503`):

  ```json
  {
    "conversationId": "<the artifact's conversation>",
    "idempotencyKey": "app-html:<artifactId>:<versionNumber>",
    "requestTitle": "<the artifact title> — app source",
    "sourceMode": "program",
    "program": {
      "language": "python",
      "sourceCode": "import base64, pathlib\npathlib.Path('/output/app.html').write_bytes(base64.b64decode('<b64>'))\n",
      "filename": "app.html"
    },
    "outputs": [{ "type": "html" }]
  }
  ```
  Two facts that decide the shape, both verified rather than assumed: the intake **requires**
  `conversationId`, `idempotencyKey` and `requestTitle` (`intake.ts:480-503`), so an App with
  `conversationId: null` (a project-linked artifact, spec §4) cannot be exported this way at all — say so in the
  card (`artifacts.app.download.unavailable`) instead of failing at the route; and `outputs` is the key the
  adapter reads for program mode (`execution-adapter.ts:253`), while the model-facing tool calls it
  `requestedOutputs` (AGENTS.md). This path costs a sandbox run and a job row.
  - **The alternative the owner is being asked about (Owner decision 7)** is a direct authenticated download of
    the stored body, and the honest facts are: the artifact download family already exists
    (`GET /api/knowledge/[id]/download`) and already answers download mode with
    `Content-Disposition: attachment` and `Cache-Control: private, no-store`
    (`file-serving-response-policy.ts:78-83`), so the bytes leave inert and the filename carries `.html` — but
    its text path hard-codes `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`
    (`knowledge/store/working-document-file-serving.ts:245-252`), because it was written for Markdown, and a
    `.html` served as `text/plain` is a cosmetic lie in a downloaded file's own metadata. It is a smaller change
    (a content-type branch) **and** it is a second download path for a generated file, which AGENTS.md forbids
    for produced files. **Recommendation: ship the program-mode export (the engine the spec names) and record
    the conversation-less case as a known gap**, rather than growing a second download route in this slice.
- **Regenerate**: ask for a new version from a new prompt; the old version is history like any other. The panel's
  own path is a **route**, mirroring Slice 1's panel-only `PATCH /api/artifacts/[id]/document/patches`:

  | Route | Request | Response |
  |---|---|---|
  | `POST /api/artifacts/[id]/app/regenerate` | `{ prompt: string, expectVersion?: number }` | `200 { ok: true, version: number, title: string, verification: AppVerification }`; `409 { ok: false, reason: "version_conflict", version: number }`; `422 { ok: false, reason: AppGenerationFailureReason, detail: string }` |

  It is `requireAuth` + scope, runs the same generator and verifier as the tool path (one implementation, two
  callers — do not fork the pipeline), and it is the only App route that writes. `expectVersion` is Slice 1's
  optimistic guard (`slice-1.md:336-340`, `PATCH /api/artifacts/[id]/body` at `:348`), not Slice 0's.
- **The card also owns the empty and error states** (UI States below): no code tab while the HTML has not
  loaded, a skeleton while the frame's document loads, the glitch line when there is one, the verification line
  when there is one, and a plain sentence when the app could not be served (404 after a delete).
- The eval harness's gallery mode is **not** shipped in the product: no debug surface renders every attempt.

trap cases).

**Serialisation with the other slices.**

1. Slice 0 first (the spine, the card, the panel, the facade, the harness skeleton, `i18n/artifacts.ts`).
2. Slice 1 next (Documents, `normal-chat-tools/artifacts.ts`, `expectVersion`, the version routes). **This slice
   assumes Slice 1 has merged** and appends to its files.
3. **This slice**, before Slices 3 and 4 (they append one line each to the same registry files).
4. Slice 5 last: it moves the artifact tools into `artifact-tools/`, so it **carries the App branch across** —
   the branch, not the tool, is this slice's. A grep for `artifactType === "app"` must find exactly one
   dispatch after the move.
5. Slices 3 and 4 touch `artifact-bodies.ts`, `ArtifactCard.svelte`, `i18n/artifacts.ts` and
   `client/api/artifacts.ts` the same append-only way, so a rebase conflict is a one-line conflict, never a
   restructure.

## UI states (1440 px and 390 px)

Tokens are Slice 0's list, all verified in `src/app.css` (`:104-137` light, `:194-224` dark):
`--surface-page`, `--surface-elevated`, `--text-primary`, `--text-muted`, `--icon-muted`,
`--border-default`, `--focus-ring`, `--accent`, `--danger`, `--radius-md`, `--radius-lg`,
`--space-sm|md|lg`, `--text-2xs|xs|sm`. No hardcoded hex, and no new token for this slice: the App body is a
card body, so it inherits the incognito remap at `src/app.css:262-266` like every other card (a literal colour
would be the one surface that ignores the incognito tint).

| State | Component | What the user sees at 1440 px | At 390 px |
|---|---|---|---|
| Loading (body fetching) | `AppBody.svelte` | `artifacts.app.generating` + `artifacts.app.generating.hint` in `--text-muted`, `--text-sm`, `aria-busy="true"`; the frame slot keeps its reserved height (`min-height: 420px`) so the reveal does not shift the conversation; **no spinner** (the chat is a reading surface) | same, `min-height: 320px` |
| Loading (frame document) | `AppFrame.svelte` | `artifacts.app.frame.loading` inside the frame's border box, `--text-muted`, `--text-sm`, centred; the `iframe` is present (so its CSP applies from the first paint) and simply has no document yet | same |
| Loaded | `AppBody.svelte` | Preview tab active: the frame fills the content column (max width the card's, not the viewport's), the app's title under it in `--text-primary` `--text-sm`, the verification line under that | tabs above the frame, full width; frame `width: 100%`, `height: min(60vh, 520px)`; the app's own document scrolls **inside** the frame, never the page (A4.7) |
| Empty (no app body stored) | `AppBody.svelte` | `artifacts.app.failed.emptyContent` in `--text-muted` plus a **Try again** action; the card keeps its header and its other actions | same, actions wrap to two rows |
| Error (body fetch failed) | `AppBody.svelte` | `artifacts.app.serve.failed` in `--danger`, `--text-sm`, with a **Try again** button ringed by `--focus-ring` and **focused on arrival** so the keyboard user is not stranded | same |
| Error 404 (artifact deleted meanwhile) | `ArtifactCard.svelte` | `artifacts.error.gone` in `--danger`; the card collapses to its header and the chat surface is untouched (no toast, no reload) — Slice 0's deleted-while-open rule | same |
| Not runnable here | `AppFrame.svelte` | `artifacts.app.frame.blocked` for a context that refuses frames (a full-page export, print); the Code tab still works | same |
| Glitch (network / storage / external) | `AppBody.svelte` | one line per `APP_GLITCH_RULE_IDS` hit, `triangle-alert` at `size={16} strokeWidth={1.75}` `aria-hidden` in `--icon-muted`, text in `--text-muted` — **not** `--danger`: the app still works, the sentence says so | same, truncated to two lines with `title=` |
| Note (design tokens missed, `note` severity) | — | **nothing shown** (Owner decision 9); the audit result is dev-only and the eval's business | nothing |
| Verification line | `AppBody.svelte` | `artifacts.app.verify.clean` / `repaired` / `uncertain` / `unavailable` in `--text-muted` `--text-xs` under the title; `uncertain` adds a `--border-subtle`-bordered note block titled `artifacts.app.verify.noteTitle` whose body is the Alfy comment, clamped to 3 lines with the full text on expand | same; the note block goes below the frame |
| Downloading | `AppBody.svelte` | the download button shows a busy state and is disabled until the produced file lands, then the File card appears in the chat (the File card is Slice 0's, not a new one) | same |
| Regenerating | `AppBody.svelte` | `artifacts.app.generating` replaces the frame's contents with the frame still mounted (so the old version is not lost if the new one fails); on failure `artifacts.app.failed.*` and the **old version keeps running** | same |
| Long title | `ArtifactCard.svelte` | one line, `overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap`, `title={title}` for the full string — Slice 0's rule, reused rather than re-decided | same |
| Long code | `AppBody.svelte` | the Code tab is a `<pre>` inside a `--radius-md` block with `overflow: auto` in **both** axes and its own scrollbar; the page never scrolls sideways; the Shiki line numbers stay in the gutter | same; the code block is the one horizontal scroll surface on the page |
| Storage refusal in the app | `AppFrame.svelte` | the frame's `onStorageError` never renders in the parent; the app shows its own localised line (`artifacts.app.storage.*` reaches the frame through the reply's `error`, the app decides). The parent shows nothing: a failed `get` is the app's business | same |

**Focus and keyboard order** (one order, both widths): card header → the tab list (`role="tablist"`, two
`role="tab"` buttons with `aria-selected`, arrow keys move between them and the panel is `aria-labelledby`) →
**the frame** (`tabindex="0"` so a keyboard user can reach it even when the app's own content has nothing
focusable; inside it the app's own order applies) → **Copy code** (Code tab only) → **Download** → **Regenerate**.
Tab moves forward, Shift+Tab back, and the frame is escapable by Tab (no focus trap anywhere). The card is not a
dialog and takes no focus on mount; the only element that takes focus on arrival is the **Try again** button in
the error state. `Enter`/`Space` activate all three actions; the regenerate dialog traps focus (it is a dialog)
and `Escape` cancels without writing.

## Failure modes

Every path has one user-visible sentence and one server answer. The strings are the A6 table's; the statuses are
the Contracts' tables.

| What went wrong | Server | User sees (EN / HU) |
|---|---|---|
| No answer / an empty fence | `generate` returns `empty_content`; **no artifact row**, so nothing to serve | `Alfy did not manage to write the app this time.` / `Alfynak most nem sikerült megírnia az alkalmazást.` |
| An answer with no `html` fence (twice) | `no_fence` | `Alfy answered, but not with a runnable app.` / `Alfy válaszolt, de nem futtatható alkalmazással.` |
| The model went looking instead of writing (twice) | `tool_call` | `Alfy tried to look around instead of writing the app. Try again.` / `Alfy írás helyett körülnézni próbált. Próbáld újra.` |
| The answer was cut off at 24 000 tokens (twice) | `too_long` | `The app grew past what can run here. Ask for something smaller.` / `Az alkalmazás nagyobb lett, mint ami itt futtatható. Kérj valami kisebbet.` |
| The turn is stopped mid-generation | the tool's abort signal reaches the model run; **no row is written** (the write is after verification) | the chat's normal stop state; nothing app-shaped appears |
| Generation exceeds the envelope budget | the tool returns its timeout error to the model, the turn continues | Alfy says it could not finish; no card |
| The verifier could not run (no Parallel key, or the model failed) | `verification: { checked: false, verdict: "unavailable" }`; the app **is** written | `Alfy could not check the facts in this app.` / `Alfy nem tudta ellenőrizni az alkalmazás adatait.` |
| The verifier is not sure | the app is written with `verdict: "uncertain"` and an `author: "alfy"` comment | `Alfy was not sure about one detail — see the note.` / `Alfy egy részletben nem volt biztos — lásd a megjegyzést.` |
| The verifier repaired the app | the repaired HTML is the version written; the finding is kept | `Alfy checked the facts and fixed one thing.` / `Alfy ellenőrizte az adatokat, és kijavított egy dolgot.` |
| The app reached for the network | the audit's `glitch` finding; the app is served anyway | `This app tried to reach the network. Everything still works offline.` / `Ez az alkalmazás hálózatot próbált elérni. Így is működik, offline.` |
| The app used `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`/IndexedDB/cookies | `glitch` (the contract forbids them, A2) | `This app used browser storage instead of Alfy's. Your data may not be kept.` / `Ez az alkalmazás a böngésző tárolóját használta Alfyé helyett. Lehet, hogy az adatok nem maradnak meg.` |
| The app linked an external resource | `glitch`; the request is blocked by the CSP, not by the app | `This app was built to load something from outside. It runs, but parts may be missing.` / `Ez az alkalmazás kívülről töltene be valamit. Fut, de egyes részei hiányozhatnak.` |
| A `set` exceeded a limit | `413` / `409` with `too_large` / `too_many_keys`; **no row written** | the app's own line: `This app tried to save more than it can.` / `Ez az alkalmazás többet próbált elmenteni, mint amennyi lehet.` |
| A `set` value cannot be serialised | `400 not_serialisable`; no row | `This app tried to save something that cannot be saved.` / `Ez az alkalmazás olyat próbált elmenteni, ami nem menthető.` |
| A frame that never replies | the bridge's timeout rejects the app's promise; the parent renders nothing | `The app could not reach its saved data.` / `Az alkalmazás nem érte el a mentett adatait.` |
| Another user's artifact | `404 { ok: false, reason: "not_found" }` on the app, kv and regenerate routes — one reason for absent, foreign and out-of-scope, so an id cannot be probed (`slice-0.md:505-506`) | `This app could not be opened.` / `Ezt az alkalmazást nem sikerült megnyitni.` |
| The artifact is deleted while the card is open | the next body fetch 404s | `artifacts.error.gone`; card collapses, chat untouched |
| Regeneration races another write | `409 version_conflict` | the dialog keeps the prompt and offers to try again |
| The app is not in a conversation | no server call at all: the action is disabled | `This app is not in a chat, so it cannot be saved as a file.` / `Ez az alkalmazás nincs beszélgetésben, ezért nem menthető fájlként.` |

## Limits and configuration

Nothing here is admin-configurable, and that is deliberate: Slice 0's `limits.ts` holds the family's caps with
the reason as its comment (`slice-0.md:922-939`), and the model/thinking/sampling values are product decisions
with a measured baseline behind them (spec §2.9, §8.1). A knob for any of them would be a knob nothing tunes.

| Cap / value | Value | Where it is read | Why not configurable |
|---|---|---|---|
| `APP_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` | `24_000` | `artifacts/app/contract.ts`, passed into the model run | The prototype's measured ceiling (2 486–3 607 completion tokens typical, one app near 24 k); `MAX_MODEL_CONTEXT` is the *provider's* window, not this call's budget, and a per-turn chat override must not shrink an app |
| `APP_SAMPLING_DEFAULTS` | temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, top_k 20 | asserted at the provider-request boundary; the values are the qwen family's `defaultSampling` (`provider-compatibility.ts:203-207`) | The prototype's values, and they are already the provider's own defaults — this slice adds **no** sampling parameter to the shared run signature |
| Thinking | pinned **off** | `APP_THINKING_MODE` in the generator, projected by `provider-model-runtime-defaults.ts` | §2.9; the alternative is an empty app, measured twice |
| `APP_KV_LIMITS` | `maxKeys` 200, `maxKeyLength` 128, `maxValueBytes` 256 KiB (all from Slice 0's `limits.ts`), `maxTotalBytes` 1 MiB (this slice) | `artifacts/app/storage.ts` | Slice 0 owns the store's caps and assigned this slice the job of surfacing them; the total is this slice's addition because the store caps a value and a count but never a total |
| Frame height reservation | `min-height: 420px` / `320px` | `AppBody.svelte` | A CLS guard, not a product value |
| `create_artifact` envelope timeout | `120_000` ms | `TOOL_TIMEOUTS_MS` (`normal-chat-tools/shared.ts:196-232`) | It must clear the App path's worst case (see A7 Step 3). **This is the one value this slice changes in a file Slices 1 and 5 also own** — reported as a conflict, and the change is one row |
| Verification call | no separate budget: the same provider path and `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` (`config-store.ts:1372`, env `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` at `env.ts:597`) that every Normal Chat model run uses | `normal-chat-model/` | Reusing the chat's provider timeout keeps one timeout story; a second one would be a second place to tune |
| `research_web` inside the verifier | its own `TOOL_TIMEOUTS_MS.research_web = 60_000` (`shared.ts:197`) | verifier tool call | Existing row, unchanged |
| Eval harness switches | `EVAL_ARTIFACTS_*`, `--suite`/`--replay`/`--limit`/`--out` (`slice-5.md:684-701`) | Slice 5's `config.ts` | The harness is not the product |

`APP_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` and `APP_SAMPLING_DEFAULTS` are the two values most likely to be questioned. They are
**not** read through `config-store.ts`, and the reason is that they are contract values: the eval suite's
baseline is only comparable to the prototype if they stay equal to it. If the owner ever wants them tunable,
the path is the standard one (`env.ts` → `config-store.ts` → settings route), and the eval's baseline has to be
re-recorded in the same change.

## Non-goals

- **No Canvas, Slides or Document work.** `artifact-bodies.ts` gains one line.
- **No in-app editing of an app's HTML**, no code editor, no "apply this snippet" — an App changes by
  regeneration (ADR-0065's exception is Documents).
- **No framework, bundler or build step in a generated app** — the contract forbids it, and the sandbox cannot
  run it.
- **No network access, ever, in the sandbox** — not for fonts, not for images, not for analytics.
- **No multi-file apps**, no asset uploads into an app, no `window.alfy` APIs beyond `storage`.
- **No sharing of an App** (spec §2.16), no public link, no embed.
- **No new dependency for highlighting** — Shiki is already here; the eval's Chromium harness reuses the
  Playwright dependency the repo already has.
- **No prompt guidance for choosing a type** (Slice 5) beyond the tool's own interface text.

## Risks

| Risk | Why it bites | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Thinking creeps back on | The whole 24k budget goes to reasoning and the user gets an empty app (measured twice) | A1.1 asserts the outgoing request with the turn's setting on; A9's live run is the end-to-end proof |
| The model's answer is not an app | No fence, prose, a partial answer, `finish_reason=length` | A1.3–A1.5 with retry and explicit failure reasons, each shown to the user in its own words |
| A wrong fact ships in a polished app | The automated verdict cannot see it — it happened in 3 of 10 | A3 flags the three real bug classes; A9's `verify` suite holds them as positives |
| The verification pass silently rewrites content | The user cannot see what changed, and a "repair" can invent a claim | A3.6–A3.7: a repair is recorded, a repair that adds a claim is `uncertain` |
| The bridge becomes a way to read another artifact | A forged message names an id and the parent obeys | A4.5: the id is the route's; A5.4: per-artifact isolation; A5.2: foreign ids 404 |
| `allow-same-origin` added for convenience | The app shares the app's origin and can call the API with the user's cookie | A4.4 asserts the exact attribute string; A4.2 asserts the exact CSP header |
| A `srcdoc` shortcut replaces the served route | No CSP header is possible on `srcdoc`, and the feature looks identical | Stated in Global Constraints with the reason; A4.2's header assertion fails if it is dropped |
| `localStorage` returning | The prototype used it; a user's app data would live where the app cannot export or erase it | The contract forbids it, A2 audits it as a **glitch**, A10.3 exports it and A10.2 erases it |
| An app's source on the stream | Every reconnect re-sends the HTML and the chat payload grows | A7.4 asserts the id only |
| The eval suite not run | §8.1's gate becomes a document nobody executes | A9 step 4 runs it on the box and its numbers go in the report beside the baseline |
| A generation wedging the turn | A long model call with no budget blocks the conversation | A7.5 asserts the budget and the model-safe failure |
| The export becomes a second, weaker runtime | The shared preview runtime trusts any `.html` with the report CSP and renders it with popups that escape (`preview-runtime/index.ts:303`, `DocumentPreviewRenderer.svelte:205-209`), while the AppFrame allows `allow-scripts` only | A6.10 asserts the download is an attachment and the card previews through the AppFrame; the outside-the-card path is recorded as a **known gap** with the policy file named (Review Focus 9) |
| The `create_artifact` timeout is missing | With no row the map lookup yields `undefined`, no timer is armed and the tool has **no timeout at all** (`shared.ts:343-350`); with Slice 1's `10_000` it aborts a healthy generation | A7.5 asserts the row is ≥ 120 s; the conflict with `slice-1.md:1000` and `slice-5.md:321` is reported |
| The kv becomes an unbounded bag | The prototype's apps write per-item keys; the store caps keys and one value but never a total | `APP_KV_LIMITS.maxTotalBytes` (1 MiB) plus A5.3's no-row assertions; Slice 0's per-key and per-value caps are imported, not restated |
| Clear Memory deletes a user's Apps | `clearMemoryAndKnowledgeForUser` deletes every artifact row whose type is not `generated_output` (`account-lifecycle/index.ts:93-97`), and an App is a `type: "artifact"` row | A10.3 asserts the real behaviour instead of the expected one, and it is raised as Owner decision 10 with the alternative (an explicit App exclusion) named |
| Verification without a Parallel key silently claims it checked | `research_web` is registered only with `parallelApiKey` present (`normal-chat-tools/index.ts:552-562`) | The `unavailable` verdict: `checked: false` is a **reported** state, and `artifacts.app.verify.unavailable` is a different sentence from `verify.clean` (Review Focus 10) |

Then, by reading rather than running:

- [ ] The E2E spec covers, end to end: ask for an app in chat; it appears only **after** verification; open it;
      use it and the state survives a reload; switch to Code and back; download the `.html` and confirm a File

      deliberately network-reaching fixture app shows its glitch message while still running.
